newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros government wins confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Comoros government wins confidence vote.

text.p: Prime Minister Ahmed Abdou of the Comoro Islands convincingly won a parliamentary confidence vote on Thursday over his handling of a secessionist revolt on Anjouan island.
Abdou's governing National Rally for Development, elected last December, won 38-2 in the federal assembly vote held after opposition parties accused it of refusing a national debate on Anjouan.
In March, several people died and hundreds were arrested on Anjouan, the Comoros' second island, after clashes between stone-throwing villagers demanding secession and troops.

The Indian Ocean Comoros, which have had 17 coups and attempted coups since independence from France in 1975, have this year been swept by a series of strikes by civil servants demanding salary arrears.
